safety_instructions.guest_instruction: During heavy rain or lightning advisories, move calmly to Indoor Hub, Theater B, Arcade Zone, or Covered Plaza and follow posted public instructions.
For urgent health needs, contact a nearby park team member or go to Care Lagoon First Aid.
Review posted height, health, and boarding requirements before joining an attraction queue.
Guests who want a quieter break may use the Indoor Hub Lower-Stimulus Corner when available.

avoidClaims: fully covered route unless every path segment is certified covered
age suitability beyond approved attraction rules
requiring staff to validate every clue
operational instruction beyond approved safety copy

noGoPairings.rule: Do not route low-sensory guests through Arcade Zone without naming Theater B or Shade Garden as an immediate reset.
Do not combine rain messaging with fully covered claims unless each path segment has covered=true and guest_route_copy allowed.
Do not write allergy or dietary content as assurance; route to staff confirmation and current menu source.
Do not use parade crossing zones during blackout windows without a timing caveat.
Do not make VIP copy imply private access, backstage access, or priority access unless supplied by a separate approved entitlement feed.

signage: six words or fewer for headline
staff_cue: defer live status to app or supervisor

blackoutWindows.reason: Theater B show seating and exit pulse

voicePrinciples: Lead with comfort and choice before novelty.
Make every route feel optional and easy to exit.
Use concrete public place names rather than vague magical language.
Keep spooky, premium, and playful concepts family-safe and pressure-free.
State review-sensitive facts as confirmation steps, not promises.
approvedPhrases: check the app for current options
ask a team member for the approved route information
pause here if this stop works better for your group
copyRules: Use public place names exactly as venue-approved.
Prefer plain language for safety, accessibility, weather, and wayfinding.
Use staff-confirmation language for allergy, medical, accessibility, ride-rule, and live-availability uncertainty.
Avoid fear-based phrasing during weather, crowd, safety, Halloween, or low-sensory guidance.
For kid quests, make the reward a memory, sticker placeholder, photo prompt, or owner-approved artifact.
